title: Exactness of inverse image on abelian sheaves and modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. The induced inverse-image functor on sheaves of abelian groups is exact. If $\mathcal B$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, the transported functor on sheaves of $\mathcal B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with scalars transported along $f^{-1}\mathcal B$, is exact on underlying abelian sheaves and therefore preserves the finite limits and cokernels used in the free-module relation presentation.

source.place: Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact, first assertion and proof (underlying inverse image of abelian sheaves is exact); the module assertion here uses transported scalars, not tensoring with a different ring.

proof.text: Give the inverse image L its Cartesian braided structure from finite-limit preservation. Regard each abelian sheaf as an internal commutative group, apply Functor.mapCommGrp, and evaluate its multiplication, unit and inverse sectionwise. Internal group diagrams give additive group laws and naturality makes restriction maps additive. Recognize the resulting presheaf as a sheaf after pulling back to a small model of the essentially small site; the underlying sheaf is unchanged. The finite-product and terminal comparison identities give the generalized-section addition and zero laws. This constructs the required abelian presentation with independent site and value universes.

For an exact functor G from an abelian category to source abelian sheaves, and an abelian-valued lift F with underlying set functor naturally isomorphic to G followed by L, the composite underlying functor preserves finite limits. Forgetting abelian sheaves preserves finite limits (sectionwise) and reflects isomorphisms, hence reflects these limits. Thus F preserves finite limits, in particular kernels and binary products. Preservation of binary products makes F additive. This applies to every presentation, without choosing an inverse-image right adjoint on abelian sheaves.

An epimorphism mapped by G remains an epimorphism and is locally surjective as a morphism of abelian sheaves. Its underlying set-sheaf map is locally surjective. The inverse-image local-family theorem applied to the singleton family shows that its image under the left adjoint L is locally surjective. Conjugating by the underlying natural isomorphism gives a locally surjective underlying map for F, hence an epimorphism. The faithful underlying functor reflects epimorphisms. Therefore F preserves epimorphisms and kernels. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology give finite-colimit preservation. Taking G to be the identity proves exactness for all abelian presentations.

Express the ring sheaf B as an internal commutative ring by its sectionwise operations. Apply the finite-product ring transport construction and evaluate its operations on each section set to build the actual transported ring sheaf LB. The ring identities follow by evaluating the internal diagrams; its sheaf condition follows on a small model. Apply the explicit imageFunctor construction of geometric module transport to obtain the module functor and underlying natural isomorphism. The Cartesian lift and terminal comparison equations give ring addition, multiplication, zero, one, module addition, zero and scalar-action normalization for every test sheaf. Finally conjugate the underlying isomorphisms by the natural ULift.down/up isomorphisms to obtain AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses with coefficient and module universe w.

For any universe-explicit module presentation, remove the harmless ULifts from its moduleUnderlying isomorphism. Apply steps 2 and 3 with G the scalar-forgetting functor on source modules and F the presented module functor followed by scalar forgetting on the target. Scalar forgetting preserves finite limits and finite colimits by the module-sheaf forgetful theorem, so this underlying abelian-valued F is exact. The target scalar-forgetting functor also reflects isomorphisms, hence reflects the finite-limit and finite-colimit comparisons. The module inverse-image functor itself is therefore exact. This proves both universal module clauses and, with step 4, the existence clause. The transported ring remains the target ring throughout; no further scalar change occurs.

Step 5: forgetting scalars preserves limits and colimits and reflects isomorphisms (proved in the step), so the module comparison maps are isomorphisms. Edge cases checked: identity morphism, zero ring, empty diagram, B=Z, non-flat ring change. No new nodes.
